objective: Make recovery completion consume typed observation evidence instead of a set difference of caller-supplied strings, so a confirmed verification after a failed attempt can only complete recovery when the ledger holds a fresh, provenance-valid observation recorded after that failure and the confirmation cites that observation's own evidence identity.
decision_supported: After a failed verification, may RecoveryLedger mark recovery COMPLETE, or must it refuse because no typed observation supports the confirmation?
acceptance: A confirmed result with no recorded observation cannot complete recovery after a failure, and the refusal names the evidence rule rather than the caller's string set.
A stale observation, an observation whose provenance did not validate, and an observation whose sequence predates the failed attempt each cannot complete recovery.
A fabricated reference not attached to the recorded observation cannot complete recovery, and is refused with its own code so an operator can tell it from a missing sample.
A fresh, provenance-valid observation recorded after the failure, whose identity the confirmation cites, completes recovery and records the completing verification id.
The gate is a sequence comparison plus set membership over typed evidence identity: it is deterministic, bounded and takes no clock-only freshness decision.
Existing RECOVERY_POLICY_EVIDENCE_NOT_FRESH behaviour for an action retry is unchanged, and the completion rule is covered by its own tests.
The legacy duplicate-string completion cases are updated to the stronger contract instead of asserting the old set difference.
Completion before any failure still needs no observation, because there is no failed attempt to answer.
No verifier rule, scenario fixture, physical control path, World Model file or contract schema is modified by this Packet.
evidence: Pre-change reproduction of the Issue #439 defect: a ledger that never called record_observation completes recovery from the string frame-fabricated, printing retry_action / None / complete confirmed None.
Post-change output of the same reproduction: the completion is refused with RECOVERY_POLICY_EVIDENCE_NOT_FRESH and the ledger state stays outside COMPLETE.
Fabricated-reference refusal output: a recorded observation carrying frame-observed and a confirmation citing frame-fabricated is refused with RECOVERY_POLICY_EVIDENCE_UNOBSERVED.
Valid fresh-stamp completion output: a fresh, provenance-valid observation at a newer sequence whose reference the confirmation cites yields state complete and the completing verification id.
Stale-stamp refusal output: the same confirmation against an observation with fresh=false is refused with RECOVERY_POLICY_EVIDENCE_NOT_FRESH.

Task Packet schema validation output for docs/task_packets/issue-439-recovery-evidence-completion.json, with exit code.

stop_conditions: Satisfying the completion rule requires reading perception directly, inventing an evidence reference, or a new evidence producer.
Satisfying the completion rule requires changing the verifier, a scenario fixture, the World Model reducer or any interfaces/ contract.
Satisfying the completion rule requires editing services/world_model/workbench_world_model/event_payloads.py, which belongs to Issue #438.
A string-only fallback would have to be accepted in production for the rule to pass, rather than a fail-closed refusal.
The rule cannot stay deterministic and bounded, or would have to introduce a clock-only freshness decision.
An existing RECOVERY_POLICY_EVIDENCE_NOT_FRESH retry case stops behaving as it does today.
The change would need to widen allowed_paths beyond the Issue #439 scope.
A required modification falls outside allowed_paths.
data_classification: internal; the tests build synthetic verification results and observation stamps and commit no real evidence
model_policy: no model call; the gate is a sequence comparison and set membership over typed evidence identity
risks_and_fallbacks: The gate could be satisfied by a string the ledger happens to hold. EvidenceStamp.evidence_refs is the observation's own identity, and the confirmation must cite one of those; a reference no observation produced has no path to completion.

Retry and completion could be conflated. A retry asks whether a sample newer than the consumed one exists, while a completion asks whether a sample newer than the failed attempt exists and is cited. They use separate watermarks so the retry loop stays finite and the completion rule stays strict.

The stricter rule could strand a run that genuinely recovered but cited an execution reference instead of the camera frame. That is a fail-closed refusal with a named code, which is the intended direction: the caller must cite the observed sample, not an actuator report.
A caller could still confirm before any failure with no observation. There is no failed attempt to answer there, so the existing behaviour is kept and the pre-failure path is not widened.

The new RECOVERY_POLICY_EVIDENCE_UNOBSERVED code is added to EMITTED_CODES so an operator can tell a fabricated reference from a missing sample. The recovery payload validator bounds reason_code by length only, so no payload schema change is needed.
observability-contract-v1.md was checked for a stated completion rule and has none, so this Packet does not modify it.
